fields.Participants: Audit Team, Board Audit Committee, CEO, CFO

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Develop Annual Audit Plan" (replaces manual Step 4).
- System auto-allocate of "Allocate audit staff and timeline in ERP/Audit Management System" (replaces manual Step 6).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: Head of Internal Audit review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **SEC revised corporate governance framework** — Audit plan must satisfy enhanced independence and scope requirements.
- **Board Audit Committee expectations and independence** — Committee may request scope changes that shift resources mid-year.
- **Revised Corporation Code requirements** — Statutory audit coverage obligations may exceed team capacity.
- **Whistleblower protection (W79 integration)** — Plan must reserve capacity for ad-hoc investigations triggered by whistleblower reports.
- Limited audit team size (~4–6) may not cover all 200 stores and 4 DCs within a single fiscal year.
Staffing Implication: Annual cycle. ~4 weeks of concentrated planning work. Requires 4–6 audit team members contributing data-gathering and survey effort. Head of IA oversees the entire process and presents to the Board Audit Committee. No dedicated additional headcount required beyond the standing audit team.
System Touchpoints: - Audit Management portal for plan creation, scheduling, and resource allocation
- Risk Register module for risk scoring and ranking
- ERP reporting: shrinkage reports (W92), margin exception reports (W85), employee turnover data
- Board portal for Audit Committee presentation and approval
- Access control reviews (SOD — Segregation of Duties matrix) as planning input
Time Estimate: ~4 weeks of dedicated planning effort (data gathering through Board approval). Quarterly updates require ~2–3 days each to refresh risk scores and adjust the audit calendar.

steps.activity: Gather data on risk indicators: shrinkage (W92), margin exceptions (W85), high turnover
Survey department heads on process risks and control weaknesses
Rank entities/processes by risk score (Impact x Likelihood)
Develop Annual Audit Plan (list of stores, DCs, and processes to be audited)
Present plan to Board Audit Committee for final approval
Allocate audit staff and timeline in ERP/Audit Management System

fields.Trigger: Approved Audit Plan (W120) or special request from CEO

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Announcement of audit" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "Test controls for POS" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documents, unauthorized overrides, stock variance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-224 (ensure audit-plan execution & remediation.)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **SEC revised corporate governance framework** — Findings must be reported with sufficient rigor to satisfy external auditors and regulators.
- **Philippine Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (RA 3019)** — Discovery of bribes or kickbacks during store audits may trigger legal obligations.
- **Board Audit Committee expectations and independence** — Committee expects timely reporting; delays erode credibility.
- **Whistleblower protection (W79 integration)** — Auditors must handle informant identities with strict confidentiality.
- **Forensic audit capability in-house vs. external** — Complex fraud cases discovered during operational audits may exceed internal team expertise.
- Store managers may be uncooperative or attempt to conceal discrepancies before unannounced audits.
Staffing Implication: 3–4 audits per month, each requiring 3–5 fieldwork days. Approximately 12–20 audit-days per month. 4–6 auditors rotating across engagements, with the Senior Auditor leading each field assignment and the Head of IA reviewing final reports. No additional headcount needed beyond the standing audit team, but peak periods (Q4 physical inventory season) may require temporary support.
System Touchpoints: - POS system logs and override records for control testing
- Inventory management module for stock variance analysis (W4)
- Petty Cash tracking system for reimbursement testing (W25)
- Audit Management portal for report storage and CAP tracking
- ERP activity logs and POS override logs for evidence capture
Time Estimate: Each audit engagement runs 3–5 fieldwork days plus 3 days report drafting, 1 week for management response, and 1 day for finalization — approximately 2–3 weeks elapsed per audit. With 3–4 audits per month, the team operates at near-full capacity year-round.

steps.activity: Announcement of audit (or unannounced for cash/inventory checks)
Fieldwork: Test controls for POS (W5), Inventory (W4), Petty Cash (W25), LP (W37)
Identify discrepancies: Missing documents, unauthorized overrides, stock variance
Exit Meeting: Discuss preliminary findings with Auditee Manager
Draft Audit Report: Categorize findings (Critical, Major, Minor)
Management Response: Auditee provides Corrective Action Plan (CAP)
Final Report Distribution & Filing in ERP

fields.Trigger: Periodic audit cycle; or "Red Flag" system alert
fields.Volume: Covers high-risk areas (Procurement, Permits, Real Estate)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "entertainment expenses, and unusual vendor credit notes" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "checks on vendors in high-risk categories" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-collect of "collection of COI disclosures from all employees in Procurement and Management" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-224 (ensure audit-plan execution & remediation.)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Philippine Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (RA 3019)** — Direct criminal liability for company officers who authorize bribe payments, even through intermediaries.
- **SEC revised corporate governance framework** — Enhanced disclosure requirements for related-party transactions and politically exposed persons (PEPs).
- **Revised Corporation Code requirements** — Director duties now include explicit anti-corruption oversight obligations.

- **Board Audit Committee expectations and independence** — Committee expects real-time escalation of red flags; delayed reporting creates governance risk. mitigated by CTL-224 (audit-plan execution & remediation)
- **Whistleblower protection (W79 integration)** — ABC red flags often originate from whistleblower tips; weak protection undermines the detection pipeline.
- **Forensic audit capability in-house vs. external** — Complex ABC cases involving foreign jurisdictions (FCPA) may require external forensic investigators.
- **DOLE involvement in employee disciplinary proceedings** — Employees terminated for corruption-related offenses may file labor cases; documentation must be legally defensible.
- **NBI coordination for criminal cases** — Corruption cases referred to the NBI require parallel internal and external investigations.
- Vendor due diligence is resource-intensive (1 day per vendor) and may bottleneck procurement for high-risk categories.
- COI disclosure compliance rate is often below 100%, especially among senior management.
Staffing Implication: Weekly red flag review takes ~2 hours per week. Quarterly ABC audit requires ~1 week of focused work. Annual training coordination (Step 5) requires ~2 weeks of preparation and delivery. The workload is handled by 1 Compliance Officer with support from Internal Audit during the quarterly audit cycle. No additional dedicated headcount required, though the Compliance Officer role itself is essential and cannot be absorbed by other positions.
System Touchpoints: - Exception reporting dashboard for red flag transaction monitoring (non-PO payments, gifts, entertainment, unusual vendor credits)
- Vendor management module for due diligence records and background check documentation
- HR module for COI disclosure collection and employee spending-authority records
- AP module for LGU permit payment audit trail (W54)
- Audit Management portal for ABC audit documentation and finding tracking
- Learning Management System (LMS) for mandatory ABC training completion records
Time Estimate: Weekly red flag review: ~2 hours/week (ongoing). Vendor due diligence: 1 day per high-risk vendor (ad-hoc, ~20–30 vendors/year). Annual COI collection: 2 weeks. Quarterly ABC audit: 1 week each (4 weeks/year). Annual training coordination: 2 weeks. Total annual effort: approximately 15–17 weeks of dedicated Compliance Officer time (2 h/wk monitoring ≈ 2.6 wk + vendor due diligence 20–30 days + COI verification 2 wk + quarterly audits 4 wk + training 2 wk), distributed across the year.

steps.activity: **Red Flag Monitoring**: Monitor high-risk transactions: non-PO payments to "consultants," gifts/entertainment expenses, and unusual vendor credit notes
**Vendor Due Diligence**: Perform background checks on vendors in high-risk categories (Construction, Government Sales)
**Conflict of Interest (COI)**: Annual collection of COI disclosures from all employees in Procurement and Management
**Audit**: Detailed audit of LGU permit payments (W54) and land acquisition fees to ensure compliance with the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) and local anti-graft laws
**Training**: Mandatory ABC training for all employees with spending authority

fields.Participants: IT Operations, Information Security, CIO, Business Process Owners
fields.Trigger: Approved Audit Plan (W120) or significant IT change (e.g., ERP migration)

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Define IT audit scope" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "Prepared by Client" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Execute Access Control testing" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: IT Auditor / Head of IA review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Highly technical scope** — Generalist auditors may lack the expertise to audit complex ERP databases or cloud infrastructure, necessitating external co-sourcing.
- **Cybersecurity risk**: A missed vulnerability during audit could lead to a significant data breach. mitigated by CTL-304 (controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1))
- **Systematic vs. manual changes** — Identifying unauthorized direct-to-database changes is difficult without specialized monitoring tools.
Staffing Implication: Annual execution. ~3–4 weeks of fieldwork and reporting. Often requires an auditor with specific IT certifications (CISA) or co-sourcing with an external audit firm.
System Touchpoints: - Active Directory / IAM for access provisioning logs
- ERP access rights and role-based permissions matrix
- IT Helpdesk & Change Management system (e.g., Jira/ServiceNow) for change approvals
- Penetration testing and vulnerability scanning reports
Time Estimate: Total elapsed time of 4–5 weeks from planning to final report.

steps.activity: Define IT audit scope (e.g., Access Management, Change Management, IT Operations, Data Backup, Cybersecurity)
Send PBC (Prepared by Client) list to IT Management
Execute Access Control testing: Verify User Access Reviews (UAR), Segregation of Duties (SOD), and termination de-provisioning
Execute Change Management testing: Sample ERP changes to verify approval, testing, and migration protocols
Assess Cybersecurity posture: Review penetration testing results, vulnerability scans, and incident response readiness
Conduct closing meeting to present preliminary findings
Issue IT Audit Report with agreed Corrective Action Plans (CAP)

fields.Volume: Hundreds of transactions evaluated; generates handful of exceptions

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-extract of "extract ERP data based on defined rules" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "generated by the CCM tool" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-route of "route valid exceptions to the respective Business Process Owner for…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: Internal Audit / Data Analyst review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **High false-positive rate** — Poorly tuned rules can overwhelm the business with exceptions, leading to "alert fatigue."
- **Data access and latency** — Extracting large volumes of data directly from the ERP without impacting production performance.
- **Integration limitations** — Disparate systems (POS, ERP, HRIS) make cross-system monitoring difficult.
Staffing Implication: Requires dedicated effort to build, tune, and monitor the scripts. Usually handled by an IT Auditor or a specialized Data Analyst within the Internal Audit team. ~10 hours per week for ongoing monitoring.
System Touchpoints: - ERP databases (direct query or BI tool extraction)
- Audit Data Analytics software (e.g., ACL, IDEA, or custom BI dashboards)
- Workflow engine to route exceptions to business owners
Time Estimate: Daily/Weekly automated execution. Exception review requires 1-2 days of analyst time per cycle.

steps.activity: Run automated scripts to extract ERP data based on defined rules (e.g., duplicate payments, POs split to avoid limits, Segregation of Duties conflicts)
Analyze exceptions generated by the CCM tool
Filter out false positives and route valid exceptions to the respective Business Process Owner for justification
Review BPO justifications; accept or escalate to a formal audit finding or investigation (W123)
Update and refine CCM rules to reduce false positives

fields.Participants: Auditees (Action Owners), Executive Team, Audit Committee
fields.Trigger: Finalized Audit Report with findings and CAPs
fields.Volume: ~50–100 open audit findings across the enterprise

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Log all findings, Corrective Action Plans" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-send of "Send automated reminders to Action Owners 14 days and 7 days prior to CAP…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-submit of "submits evidence of remediation to Internal Audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-224 (ensure audit-plan execution & remediation.)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Remediation delays** — Business units often deprioritize audit fixes in favor of operational tasks, leading to aging issues.
- **"Band-aid" fixes** — Business owners may implement superficial fixes that pass the immediate re-test but fail to address the root cause.
- **Manual tracking** — Using spreadsheets instead of a dedicated GRC tool makes tracking 100+ findings across 200 stores highly error-prone.
Staffing Implication: Continuous activity. Requires ~10–15% of the audit team's total capacity for follow-up testing and reporting.
System Touchpoints: - Audit Management System / GRC Tool for issue tracking and evidence repository
- BI Dashboards for real-time visibility into open/overdue issues
Time Estimate: Monthly status checks (~1 day). Quarterly Audit Committee reporting preparation (~2–3 days). Follow-up testing takes 2-5 days per batch of closed issues.

steps.activity: Log all findings, Corrective Action Plans (CAPs), owners, and due dates into the Audit Management System
Send automated reminders to Action Owners 14 days and 7 days prior to CAP deadline
Action Owner submits evidence of remediation to Internal Audit
Perform follow-up testing (re-audit) to validate that the control is operating effectively
Close finding if validated; escalate to Executive Team if CAP is delayed or evidence is insufficient
Generate quarterly Open Issues Report for the Board Audit Committee, highlighting overdue high-risk findings

fields.Trigger: Annual audit plan or high-risk vendor onboarding

steps.activity: Identify critical vendors (IT services, data hosting, major supply chain partners)
Request and review SOC 2 reports, ISO 27001 certifications, and SLA performance
Conduct on-site or remote vendor control audit and process walkthrough
Evaluate data privacy compliance (DPA) and IT security practices of vendor
Issue Vendor Audit Report with identified control gaps and remediation requests
Track vendor CAPs; suspend vendor contract if critical vulnerabilities remain unresolved

fields.Frequency: Annual internal review, every 5 years external assessment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitoring of internal audit performance metrics" (replaces manual Step 1).

steps.activity: Perform ongoing monitoring of internal audit performance metrics (e.g., plan completion rate, report turnaround time)
Conduct annual self-assessment of the audit activity against IIA standards and Code of Ethics
Review audit workpapers for a sample of engagements to ensure quality and compliance with methodology
Solicit feedback from auditees post-engagement via surveys
Engage an independent external reviewer every 5 years for a full Quality Assessment Review (QAR)
Present QAIP results and action plans to the Board Audit Committee

fields.Participants: Payroll Manager, HR Manager, Finance, external tax advisor
fields.Trigger: Annual audit plan or high turnover/grievance alerts

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Perform ghost employee testing" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "Verify basic, OT, night diff, and holiday pay accuracy" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-reconcile of "Reconcile payroll deductions to SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG payments" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: Internal Audit review and approval gate; periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ghost employees** — Deliberate creation of fictitious profiles to siphon funds.

- **Statutory under-remittance** — Risk of massive penalties and legal action from government agencies. mitigated by the Internal Audit review and approval gate and periodic reconciliation against source documents

- **Labor Code violations** — Incorrect holiday or OT pay leading to DOLE complaints and class-action risk. mitigated by the Internal Audit review and approval gate and periodic reconciliation against source documents
Staffing Implication: Annual execution. Handled by 1 Senior Auditor + 1 Junior Auditor. Peak effort during Q1 (post-13th month pay).
System Touchpoints: - Payroll module for transaction history and master data
- Biometric T&A system for attendance verification
- Finance/AP module for remittance payment confirmation
Time Estimate: ~3 weeks total elapsed (1 week prep/sampling, 1 week fieldwork, 1 week reporting).

steps.activity: Select a sample of employees across different entities and levels (Store, DC, HQ)
Perform ghost employee testing: Verify physical existence of sampled employees vs. payroll records
Re-calculate payroll for a sample period: Verify basic, OT, night diff, and holiday pay accuracy
Audit statutory remittances: Reconcile payroll deductions to SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG payments
Review 13th month pay and bonus calculations for compliance with Philippine Labor Code
Verify BIR 2316 issuance and Alphalist accuracy (W90)
Issue Payroll Audit Report with findings and remediation plans

fields.Participants: IT Manager, Business Process Owners (BPO), CIO
fields.Trigger: Semi-annual review or major system change

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-assign of "Extract User-Role matrix from ERP showing all assigned permissions" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-create of "create Vendor AND approve Payment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Review exceptions with Business Process Owners" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: IT Auditor / Head of IA review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Excessive access** — Users accumulating roles over time ("permission creep").
- **Collusion risk**: Single user having end-to-end control over a financial cycle. mitigated by the IT Auditor / Head of IA review and approval gate
- **Manual mitigation** — Relying on "trust" instead of system-enforced controls.
Staffing Implication: Semi-annual cycle. Led by IT Auditor with support from BPOs. IT Admin effort for execution.
System Touchpoints: - GRC Tool or SOD reporting scripts
- Audit logs for monitoring "High Risk" transaction usage
Time Estimate: 2-3 weeks elapsed per cycle.

steps.activity: Extract User-Role matrix from ERP showing all assigned permissions
Run SOD conflict report against defined conflict matrix (e.g., User can create Vendor AND approve Payment)
Triage identified conflicts: Distinguish between "True Conflict" and "Mitigated Risk"
Review exceptions with Business Process Owners; define remediation (remove access) or mitigation (manual supervisor review)
IT executes access removal/changes in the system
Document mitigating controls for accepted risks (e.g., dual-auth on high-value POs)
Final SOD Compliance Report presented to CIO and Audit Committee

workflows.name: Regulatory Compliance Audit (DPA, Labor, Consumer Act)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs, consent forms, and PII access logs" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Verify price tag display, return policy compliance, and DTI permit usage" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System continuous audit of "Audit Labor Code" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: Compliance Officer / Internal Audit review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **NPC Fines** — Non-compliance with DPA can lead to revenue-based fines.
- **DTI/DOH Sanctions** — Product liability or promotion violations.
- **Closure orders** — Lapsed LGU permits.

steps.activity: Audit Data Privacy (RA 10173): Review DSAR logs, consent forms, and PII access logs (W271)
Audit Consumer Act (RA 7394): Verify price tag display, return policy compliance, and DTI permit usage (W427/W69)
Audit Labor Code: Verify minimum wage adherence, work hour limits, and safety standards (W140)
Verify LGU permit currency (W54) and BIR CAS compliance (W216)
Conduct field visits to sample stores to verify physical compliance (signage, safety equipment)
Issue Consolidated Regulatory Compliance Report

fields.Trigger: Random selection or high-shrinkage/cash variance alerts (W37)

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Auditor arrives at store unannounced" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Count cash in vault, petty cash float, and all active registers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "reports from POS and vault balances from ERP" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: Internal Audit / Loss Prevention review and approval gate; periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Kiting** — Temporary "borrowing" of cash by staff, replaced before scheduled counts.
- **Vault access control** — Unauthorized users having safe combinations/keys.
- **Manual log manipulation** — Falsifying CIT logs to hide shortages.
Staffing Implication: Monthly rotational. 1 Auditor per store visit. Conducted unannounced by Audit or LP team members.
Time Estimate: 4-6 hours per store visit.

steps.activity: Auditor arrives at store unannounced; immediately secures the vault and cash registers
Count cash in vault, petty cash float, and all active registers
Pull real-time "Cash-in-Drawer" reports from POS and vault balances from ERP
Reconcile physical count vs. system balance; identify shortages/overages
Verify CIT pickup logs and bag seals against system records (W174)
Review manager overrides for the last 7 days: Voids, refunds, price changes
Finalize Audit Memo; obtain Store Manager acknowledgment

fields.Participants: DC/Store Operations, Inventory Control, External Auditors
fields.Trigger: Annual physical inventory (W42) or high-shrinkage alerts (W37)
fields.Volume: All 4 DCs and sample of 20–30 high-risk stores

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Verify that the “Cut-off” is clean" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "counting teams to ensure they follow the approved SOP" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-test of "Perform independent test counts of high-value or" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-304 (ensure controlled execution — Audit Planning & Execution (PA-21.1).)
- operational: Internal Audit review and approval gate; periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cut-off Errors** — In-transit stock or unposted receipts causing phantom variances.
- **Blind Counting Failures** — Count teams having access to "system quantities" during count.
- **Theft during Count** — High-value items being moved or hidden during the physical count.
Time Estimate: ~6–7 audit-days per full-count cycle (cut-off verification 1 day + count observation 1–2 days + independent test counts 4 hours + reconciliation review 1 day + system posting audit 1 day + shrinkage-classification root-cause audit 2 days) ≈ 48–56 hours across the 4 DCs and the 20–30 sampled high-risk stores; quarterly cycle-count audits run a reduced subset of the same steps (annual full counts).

steps.activity: **Pre-Count Audit**: Verify that the "Cut-off" is clean (no pending GRs or Shipments) and area is organized
**Observation**: Observe the counting teams to ensure they follow the approved SOP (W42)
**Test Counts**: Perform independent test counts of high-value or high-variance SKUs
**Reconciliation Review**: Verify that all count sheets are uploaded and variances are investigated before posting
**System Posting Audit**: Confirm that final adjustments are correctly posted to the GL (W92)
**Root Cause Analysis**: Audit the shrinkage classification for accuracy (W37)

workflows.name: Lease & CAM (Common Area Maintenance) Compliance Audit

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Extract lease terms: base rent, escalation clauses, and CAM/Utility formula" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-calculate of "calculate rent and escalations vs." (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify pro-rata share calculations" (replaces manual Step 3).

- operational: Internal Audit / Real Estate Compliance review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overpayment of CAM** — Landlords including non-allowable expenses in the CAM pool.
- **Escalation Errors** — Complex multi-tier escalation formulas applied incorrectly.
- **Sales Under-reporting** — Risk of landlord penalties if POS data doesn't match reported sales. mitigated by the Internal Audit / Real Estate Compliance review and approval gate
Time Estimate: 9 days elapsed per occurrence (1 day + 2 days + 3 days + 2 days + 1 day); cadence-carried steps as authored (Ongoing) — at Annual (rotational across store portfolio) ≈ 1 occurrence/year.

steps.activity: **Contract Review**: Extract lease terms: base rent, escalation clauses, and CAM/Utility formula from Legal (W230)
**Payment Recalculation**: Re-calculate rent and escalations vs. actual payments in ERP (W7)
**CAM Audit**: Request and audit landlord's CAM breakdown; verify pro-rata share calculations
**Sales-Percentage Rent Audit**: Verify that "Gross Sales" reported to landlord matches POS records
**Utility Surcharge Review**: Verify that landlord electricity/water markups comply with lease terms
**Recovery Claim**: Issue formal demand to landlord for overcharges identified

steps.activity: **Pricing Consistency Audit**: Verify price/promo parity between POS and digital channels (W2237)
**Fulfillment Audit**: Audit last-mile delivery success rates and return/refund accuracy (W19)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs from ERP to BIR 2550 forms" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Withholding Tax Audit" (replaces manual Step 2).
